what: Finding 1: proposed design-publish.sh invokes render-final-summary.sh from parsed argv but does not require exporting ISSUE_NUMBER and SESSION_ID from --issue and --session-id.
scenario_or_breakage: render-final-summary.sh reads DESIGN_TMPDIR, SESSION_ID, and ISSUE_NUMBER from environment; if the new driver relies only on argv, final-summary.md can show run unknown or Issue N/A and skip the larch:final-summary upsert.
suggested_fix: In design-publish.sh export SESSION_ID and ISSUE_NUMBER="$ISSUE" after argv validation and before every render-final-summary.sh call; add a harness assertion that the render stub sees both env vars.

what: Finding 2: the plan drops the current branch for design-log-publish.sh exiting nonzero without any PUBLISH_OK line.
scenario_or_breakage: If design-log-publish.sh crashes before emitting PUBLISH_OK, PUBLISH_OK stays empty; rename is skipped, but the failure is no longer treated as the current unexpected shell failure and may not be recorded in Warnings.
suggested_fix: Port the exact current capture semantics: parse stdout regardless of rc, and when rc is nonzero with no PUBLISH_OK line, handle it as an unexpected publish failure, append design-log-publish.failure.log under Warnings, keep cleanup skipped, and cover this case in test-design-publish.sh.

what: Finding 3: the SKILL.md rewrite description is internally inconsistent about emitting final-summary.md on PLAN_WRITE_OK=false.
scenario_or_breakage: The plan-block-write failure path currently renders and emits the failed-plan-write summary before the warning; the proposed SKILL rewrite text only says to apply the shared full-body emit on success, so an implementer could print only the warning and skip the failure summary.
suggested_fix: Make the Step 5c post-driver branch explicitly emit FINAL_SUMMARY_PATH for both PLAN_WRITE_OK=false and PLAN_WRITE_OK=true before the warning/footer decision; keep the success-only 5c.5 status line separate.

what: Finding 4: the plan resolves REPO before plan-block-write even though current Step 5c failure handling explicitly skips REPO resolution after a plan-block-write failure.
scenario_or_breakage: On a plan-block-write failure, the extracted driver may perform an extra gh repo view before the write/failure path; that is scope creep for a pure extraction and changes the current skip condition around GitHub-facing work.
suggested_fix: Keep the current order: run plan-block-write.sh first with no --repo; on failure render using only any already-supplied REPO, then exit; resolve REPO only after PLAN_WRITE_OK=true before diagram upsert/publish/rename.
